Ordering of mixtime vectors

Source: R/compare.R
mixtime-order.Rd

sort() and xtfrm() (which powers order() and rank()) order a mixtime vector chronologically. A discrete time (e.g. yearmonth("2020 Jan")) is a span rather than an instant, so ordering it against time of another chronon first picks an instant within the span.

align_discrete sets that instant: 0 for the start of the span, 1 for its end, and 0.5 (the default) for its midpoint. It only changes the order of time with different chronons; time sharing a chronon keeps its order.

xtfrm() takes no other arguments, so order(), rank() and vctrs ordering always use the midpoint. Use sort() to choose another instant.

Usage

## S7 method for class <mixtime::mixtime>
xtfrm(x)

## S7 method for class <mixtime::mixtime>
sort(x, decreasing = FALSE, na.last = NA, ..., align_discrete = 0.5)

Arguments

x, decreasing, na.last, ...

See sort().

align_discrete

The position within a discrete time span used to order it against time of another chronon, from 0 (start) to 1 (end).

Value

sort() returns a mixtime vector; xtfrm() returns a numeric vector suitable for ranking.

Examples

x <- c(yearmonth("2020 Jan"), date("2020-01-20"), yearmonth("2020 Feb"))
sort(x)
#> <mixtime[3]>
#> [1] 2020 Jan   2020-01-20 2020 Feb  
# January ends after the 20th
sort(x, align_discrete = 1)
#> <mixtime[3]>
#> [1] 2020-01-20 2020 Jan   2020 Feb  
sort(x, decreasing = TRUE)
#> <mixtime[3]>
#> [1] 2020 Feb   2020-01-20 2020 Jan
